entry.title: Head of Alexander the Great
entry.blurb: After his death, Alexander was worshiped as a god; posthumous portraits like this one, likely carved in Ptolemaic Egypt, portray him with long hair and youthful, idealized features.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Gift of Mrs. Ralph King

facts: Slightly smaller than life-size, this head of Alexander the Great features a slight turn, tilt, and upward gaze said to have characterized the young conqueror's posture in life.
Portraits of Alexander the Great share his characteristic anastole hairstyle, parted off-center and swept back from the forehead.
